standard_prerequisites.name: Two-row standard Young tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: For lambda = (N-k_1,k_1) the superstandard tableau T_lambda fills the first row with the odd numbers and the second row with the even numbers up to 2k_1, and the rest in the first row.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof identifies row_2(T) with the even numbers {2,4,...,2k_1} using precisely this filling.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent set and odd numbers
standard_prerequisites.statement: Des(T) is the set of i with i+1 in a lower row than i, and odds(k_1) = {1,3,...,2k_1-1}.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is Des(T_lambda) = odds(k_1), and the proof reads the row membership off from that equality.

core_obligations: Dispose of the first assertion, which is immediate from the two-row superstandard filling (source line 598).
For the second, take T in Syt(mu) with Des(T) = Des(T_lambda) and reduce to showing row_2(T) = row_2(T_lambda), since both tableaux have two rows (source line 608).
From Des(T) = {1,3,...,2k_1-1} deduce that all odd numbers up to 2k_1-1 lie in row 1 and all even numbers up to 2k_1 lie in row 2, hence 2k_1+1 lies in row 1 (source line 608).
Since T has no descents past index 2k_1-1, every entry larger than 2k_1 must also lie in row 1, so row_2(T) = {2,4,...,2k_1} and therefore k_1 = k_2 and T = T_lambda (source line 608).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the agreement of the second rows.
Read the second row off from the descent set and the absence of later descents.
Conclude the equality of shapes and of tableaux.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:superstandard two rows characterize coefficients` at source lines 594-601: for two-row shapes lambda = (N-k_1,k_1) and mu = (N-k_2,k_2) the descent set of the superstandard tableau is the odd set odds(k_1), and any two-row tableau with that descent set must coincide with T_lambda, in particular forcing k_1 = k_2. The author's proof (source lines 605-609) is short but it is a genuine argument about the shape: after reducing to the equality of the second rows (line 608), it uses the descent set to place all odd numbers up to 2k_1-1 in the first row and all even numbers up to 2k_1 in the second, deduces that 2k_1+1 is in the first row, and then uses the absence of descents beyond index 2k_1-1 to force every larger entry into the first row, which pins the second row completely. The statement gives only the cardinality-free uniqueness clause.
